edges.description: Loss of wall integrity can progress from dilatation to rupture with hematoma, gastrointestinal bleeding, or shock.
Increased flow and wall stress can drive remodeling of the splenic arterial wall.
Local geometry-driven stress can promote focal dilatation.
Pregnancy-related hemodynamic and hormonal stress increases concern for rupture.

The node is named for this exposure and describes the flow state it produces, so the two are the same claim seen from either end. The first item is the stronger, proposing the hyperkinetic splenic state as the route from portal hypertension to the aneurysm, which is the node itself rather than the disease.

Graded below the portal hypertension link into this same node, and the reason is that the evidence is really about portal hypertension rather than about transplantation: within a transplant series, aneurysms were found in 16 percent of patients with portal hypertension and in none without it. The transplant setting is where the observation was made, not what the observation is of.
edges.source: Liver transplantation and parenchymal liver disease context

edges.description: The formation arm of this exposure, added after review pointed out that this entry already holds the sentence for it. Hormonal influence and gestational changes in portal flow are what this node is made of, and the cited sentence names both as believed to matter in development of the aneurysm. Graded partial because it is believed rather than shown, which is what that grade is for. Drawing it also repairs a structural gap: without it the exposure jumped past its own mechanism node to rupture, leaving the two disconnected.

Pointed at rupture because that is what the two sentences carried here establish: mortality after rupture in pregnancy, and a female preponderance of incidental findings attributed to obstetric ultrasonography. Neither of those speaks to how an aneurysm forms. That is a statement about these two sentences and not about the source, which does also address formation; that arm is drawn as the separate link into the pregnancy-stress node above, so the exposure now reaches both its mechanism and its consequence.

Pointed at arterial wall remodeling rather than at the portal hyperkinetic node, because the whole interest of this exposure is that it operates in patients without portal hypertension, by a systemic pressure route rather than a splanchnic flow one. Graded partial because the supporting cohort is twelve patients.
